summary: Windows IOCP step() previously polled once without waiting, processing at most one completion. Outstanding operations could retain unfired wakers, leaving async callers pending indefinitely. The fix loops until all tracked operations are reaped, using 10 ms completion waits while preserving nonblocking drain(). The added regression queues 64 writes and checks every completion and waker after one step(). The reversal restores step(), the completion-processing signature, and its callers together. This test requires Windows with the experimental_win_iocp feature and normal filesystem support; it will not execute on Linux. No builds or tests were run.
